title: Broncos Face Jaguars Seeking First Win of the Season
seoTitle: Broncos face Jaguars in Denver seeking season's first win
subtitle: Everything fans need to know to follow the showdown in Denver
excerpt: Denver hosts Jacksonville this Sunday for NFL Week 2. Find out where to watch, key players, and what experts expect from the matchup.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Denver Broncos, Sports Illustrated, Mile High Report
contentHtml:
The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars this Sunday, September 20, at Empower Field at Mile High, seeking their first win of the season. The matchup has garnered attention because the Jags defeated Denver in the last game between the two teams.

How to Watch the Game at Home and Away

For those in the United States, the local broadcast will be on CBS, with Ian Eagle on play-by-play and Ross Tucker as analyst. The same game can be streamed on NFL+ or Paramount+, which allow live viewing on mobile devices.

Options for Those Outside the United States

Those not in American territory can use NFL Sunday Ticket, available on YouTube or YouTube TV, to watch all out-of-market games. International viewers have access to NFL GamePass International.

What Experts Say About the Matchup

Sports Illustrated analysts point out that, despite the Broncos being favorites, the Jaguars have a good chance to surprise, especially after their Week 1 victory. The consensus indicates that the Jags can exploit Denver's defensive vulnerability, which struggled against the Chiefs in the opener.

Injuries That Could Influence the Outcome

The Broncos' injury report indicates that running back RJ Harvey is limited by a thigh injury and wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. is out. These absences could reduce offensive options for Denver.

Key Individual Standouts

Trevor Lawrence, Jaguars quarterback, completed 18 of 23 passes in the win over the Cleveland Browns, accumulating 245 yards and four touchdowns. On the other hand, Bo Nix, of the Broncos, is still looking to establish himself after the loss against the Chiefs.

Where to Listen to the Game Live

On local radio, the broadcast will be on KOA 850 AM/94.1 FM, with Dave Logan on play-by-play. Those who prefer national audio can tune into ESPN Radio, with Roxy Bernstein as announcer.

With information from Denver Broncos, Sports Illustrated, Mile High Report.
